system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
PHYSICS CHECK — governing physical relation: Nernst equation and proton conductivity dependence on membrane hydration. At 1.5 A/cm² current density, proton conductivity drops sharply when membrane water content falls below λ=2 (water molecules per sulfonic acid group), causing ionic resistance increase and hot spot formation. Current density must be balanced by water generation rate to maintain membrane hydration.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — components: (1) Anode water injection system with micro-pump and flow control valve, (2) Humidity sensor array at anode inlet/outlet and within stack (3 control zones), (3) Stack voltage monitoring circuit with 10 mV resolution, (4) Temperature sensor array (1 per 5 cells). Materials: Nafion membrane, PTFE tubing, 316L stainless steel injection nozzles. Procedure: Install injection system upstream of anode inlet, calibrate humidity sensors, implement control logic to inject water when anode outlet humidity drops below 60% or stack voltage deviation exceeds 50 mV from average.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — Implementation burden is moderate (additional pump and sensors) but comparable to existing cathode humidification systems. Operability is similar to current systems with added control complexity. Maintenance requires periodic filter replacement for injection system. Cost class is similar to standard cathode humidification (off-the-shelf components), but avoids the 10% parasitic load penalty by utilizing waste water from anode exhaust.
EXECUTIVE TEST — falsification test protocol: Operate fuel cell stack at 1.5 A/cm², 80°C, with anode humidity control system active. Monitor stack voltage, temperature distribution, and anode humidity for 2 hours. Pass threshold: Stack voltage variation < 100 mV peak-to-peak, maximum temperature deviation < 5°C from average, anode outlet humidity maintained > 60%. Fail threshold: Any single cell voltage drop > 200 mV, temperature hot spot > 10°C above average, or anode outlet humidity < 50% sustained for > 5 minutes. Test duration: 2 hours.
